title: Harness engineering: Managing tool access, error handling, and safety
text: Then looked at the result before the next move. That looking is what makes it an agent. Now the tell. A chatbot, you ask, it answers, done. One turn, no tools, it never sees a result. An agent, it acts, observes, and decides again and again until it's finished. So, ask two questions of any so-called agent. Where's the loop and who owns the stop condition? No loop, no observation, it's a chatbot with a costume on. And here's why the harness matters. It's the part you actually build and control. Which tools it can reach, when it's allowed to stop, what happens when a tool errors, how much it remembers. The model gets the headlines, but the harness is where the

Real engineering and the real safety lives. So, next time someone says agent, run the test. It's a model in a loop with tools that acts and observes until it's done. Ask where the loop is and who owns the stop. That's the harness and that's the part that's really yours. Your turn and this is a real exercise. Take a task you do in steps, say triaging your inbox. Write down the tools an agent would need and the exact rule for when it should stop. That stop condition is the hardest part and writing it is how you learn what a harness really does. Agent harness, a model in a loop with tools that acts until it's done. Humanitarian's AI.
